    Kisiei–English dictionary¶

    This dictionary is generated automatically from the project's lexicon (4250 entries). Words follow the Kisiei alphabetical order (ɛ after e, ŋ and ɲ after n, ɔ after o); tone marks are ignored for sorting. The underline of each word shows its source, as elsewhere in this guide: Attested in the Bible (with a reference to one occurrence), Confirmed by a speaker, Respelled from Keita 1979, To check, or Southern Kissi (Childs 2000 only, not attested in the North). To look up a word from English, see the English–Kisiei index; for words grouped by theme, see the word lists. The full lexicon is also available as CSV, TSV, LIFT and CLDF in the repository.

    A¶

    aa part. — quotative particle. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): also 'like, as' (comparison). Gen 1:3

    akasia n. — acacia (pɛngɛn akasia 'acacia wood'). Exod 25:10

    -àlè part. — Southern Kissi only — emphatic tag (after commands, greetings). Childs 2000, p. 2

    amanndiee n. — almond, almond tree (yɔm amanndiee). Num 17:23

    ansan n. — incense. Exod 25:6

    a yandi interj. — please.

    a1 prep. — with; and. Gen 1

    a2 pron. — you (sg.); they (subject). Gen 1

    yɔŋnun v. — become, be; happen. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): happen, occur; become. Other forms: yɔŋnunnin, yɔŋnɔn. Gen 1:5

    yɔŋɔɔ n. — gift, present. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): (verb) send (something), present, offer; cf. yɔ̀ŋndó 'gift, sending'. Gen 33:11

    yɔŋulɔnndo n., pl. yɔŋulɔnnda — wound, injury; (yɔŋulannda) the wounded. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): harming oneself (middle plural of yɔ̀ŋùlló 'harm'). Other forms: yɔŋulɔn, yɔŋulɔnndan, yɔŋulannda. Deut 17:8

    yɔŋul v. — injure, harm, wound. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): poison, wound, harm. Lev 24:19

    yɔ̀ɔ̀máá n. (o), pl. yɔ̀ɔ̀méí — Southern Kissi only — tree species used for rafters. Childs 2000, p. 415

    yɔɔn n. — thorns. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): thorn, splinter (singular yùéí). Gen 3:18

    yɔɔɲɔɔ n. (o) — pangolin. Keita 1979, p. 138

    yɔɔsɔɔ n., pl. yɔɔsɔla — thread, yarn (for weaving); (kola-yɔɔsɔɔ) weaver's beam. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): thread of traditional woven cloth; also a young palm tree. Exod 25:4

    yɔ́ɔ́sɔ́ɔ́ n. (o), pl. yɔ́ɔ́súáŋ — Southern Kissi only — young or short palm tree. Childs 2000, p. 416

    yɔɔvaa n. (o) — bead necklace, beads. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): beads worn around the neck or the waist. Ezek 16:11

    yɔɔyaa v. — fish. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): fish (with a net). Other forms: yɔɔya. Lev 11:18

    yɔ̀ɔ̀yɔ̀ɔ́ n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — Adam's apple; double chin; wattles. Childs 2000, p. 416

    yɔɔ v. — lead, take along, bring; shepherd (saa yɔɔ diólan). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): take, bring, carry. Ezek 34:23

    yɔ́ɔ́ n. (o), pl. yɔ́léŋ — Southern Kissi only — edible green (for palaver sauce). Childs 2000, p. 415

    yɔwviaa n. — make-up (Keita). Keita 1979, p. 145

    yùèŋndéŋ n. (le) — Southern Kissi only — pimple. Childs 2000, p. 416

    yùfúáánɔ̀ɔ́ n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — virgin. Childs 2000, p. 416

    yúkòó n. (o), pl. yúkùá — Southern Kissi only — nephew. Childs 2000, p. 416

    yulalen n. (len) — trade, commerce (tosa yulalen 'trade'). Other forms: yulale. Ezek 27:12

    yulanɔɔ n. (o) — trader, merchant. Isa 24:2

    yulan-yulanndo n. — trembling, terror, confusion. Other forms: yulan-yulan, yulan-yulanndan. Lev 26:16

    yùléŋ n. (le) — Southern Kissi only — tree species with red sap (used to weaken boas). Childs 2000, p. 416

    yulɔɔ v. — bear, endure. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): smoke out; point at; be patient, withstand pain; stretch. 1 Thess 3:1

    yúlúlló n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — edible mushroom species with a long root. Childs 2000, p. 416

    yulul v. — draw, aim (a bow) at. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): smoke out, point (at) for someone; be patient. Ps 7:13

    yulunnde n. — grey hair; old age. Prov 16:31

    yulu v. — stretch out (the hand, a staff). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): smoke out; point at; be patient; stretch. Exod 7:19

    yumbuyumboo n. (o) — cloud, clouds. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): fog. Other forms: yumbuyumbu. Gen 9:14

    yúnɛ̀ɛ̀ ideo. — Southern Kissi only — (sound heard from far away). Childs 2000, p. 417

    yungaa v. — plunder, despoil, strip. Other forms: yunga, yunganin. Gen 14:11

    yungoo n. (o), pl. yungulan — family, household; people (of a place) ; family, household; people, nation. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): family, household; also a cooking tripod, hearth. Other forms: yungu, yungula. Gen 7:1

    yùŋàá v. — Southern Kissi only — strip off, pluck; clean (an animal). Childs 2000, p. 417

    yúŋgàá n. — Southern Kissi only — skin disease (humans and animals), dandruff. Childs 2000, p. 417

    yùŋgòó n. — Southern Kissi only — egg yolk. Childs 2000, p. 417

    yùŋgùláŋ n. (la) — Southern Kissi only — dust produced by wood bugs or termites. Childs 2000, p. 417

    yùŋòó n. — Southern Kissi only — soft, mushy state (overcooked tuber). Childs 2000, p. 417

    yùŋɔ̀ɔ́ n. (o), pl. yùŋéláŋ — Southern Kissi only — fish trap, fish fence across a river. Childs 2000, p. 417

    yúŋúlló n. (o), pl. yúŋúltáŋ — Southern Kissi only — shaved or bald head. Childs 2000, p. 417

    yuuluo n. (o), pl. yuululan — rag. Keita 1979, p. 145

    yùùlútààmɔ̀ɔ́ n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — cloth worn by women during menstruation. Childs 2000, p. 418

    yuunda v. — take away, strip off (someone's clothes). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): remove or strip, scrape clean. Hos 2:11

    yuuvaa v. — grow old, be old. Other forms: yuuva. Josh 23:2

    yuuvɛiyo n. (o), pl. yuuvɛiya — old age; old person. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): (adjective) old. Other forms: yuuvɛi. Gen 42:38
